description:
What is Gelato vs Ice Cream?

That's a question that's been floating around for years but have the lines been crossed recently?

Every time you go to a scoop shop or even your local supermarket, you find Gelato. It's the new "fad" outside of Italy (who have always sold it). In Italy, there are laws regarding what Gelato can and can't be, the same can't be said for elsewhere in the world. 

In this weeks video, we dive a little in to the difference and make some of each. We also use Sakura Coffee from Anorak Coffee (not affiliated) which is linked here:
https://www.anorakcoffee.co.uk/online-store/Sakura-p119460095
It's really quite nice but likely only available in the UK. You can also visit their Instagram page here: https://www.instagram.com/coffeeanorak/?hl=en

If you want to try these recipes (with or without the Sakura Coffee), the recipes are below:

Gelato:
700g Milk 
150g Double/Heavy Cream
180g Sugar
65g SMP
1 Egg yolk
1g Stablizer
(Coffee Granules if required)

Ice Cream:
500g Milk
425g Double/Heavy Cream
190g sugar
50 SMP
1 Egg yolk
(Coffee granules if required)

Making Gelato does really need a gelato specific machine as mentioned in the video but you can achieve something close at home. 

We hope you enjoy this weeks video and don't forget to like and subscribe so you don't miss our next episode of the Chocolate Series.

comments.text:
Lets be honest what Gelato is there is 3 core things compare to Ice Cream or American Ice Cream.
1. Fat content (higher fat content is muting flavor and sweetness). Meaning if 2 style of frozen dessert have the same amount of sugars they will still have a different mouthfeel and sweetness. Some part of Italy do not like cold mouthfeel of a frozen dessert so they prefer more fat. 
2. Air content (higher air content have less density). Meaning if 2 style of frozen dessert have different amount of air the concentration will be different. Same amount of sugars will not have same amount of mouthfeel and sweetness.
3. Serving temperature (lower serving temperature will release flavor slowly). Meaning if 2 style of frozen dessert have different serving temperature they will release flavor and sweetness differently. Its when something melt we get a concentration of flavor and sweetness. Most Artisanal Gelato shops in Italy only store the base for 3 days it means they could use fresh fruits, natural ingredients. 

There is no law in Italy what Artisanal Gelato is. On other hand there is law in US what Ice Cream is.

Anyone who really like to taste good Artisanal Gelato should visit Rome.

comments.text: For a cheap home machine it is better if one uses a gelato recipe. Some of the best gelatos in Italy have 10% overrun only. This is best achieved in a home with the dinky little cheap machine funnily enough! The very old cipriani machines in Italy are so sought after because they are the only ones that can do that. But you have to pasteurise and cool the mix by hand. The new machines that do that automatically, but produce 20-30% overrun.

comments.text:
Ah well you see the numbers for an ice cream / gelato recipe are relative. The gelato recipe has less sugar at 180g but a higher percentage overall in the finished recipe, I will check I’ve put the correct numbers down though ☺️. The use of an ice cream calculator (I’m going through one in next weeks video) shows the percentage breakdowns. 
Gelato can easily have half the fat of ice cream, if made correctly, the result of gelato is amazing and gives no noticeable ice crystals at the correct serving temperature (which is slightly higher). 
As for machine, Nemox make an adjustable machine but it not cheap at all. 
To most people, the difference is minor but to those that make it, the difference is HUGE! 😊
